questions.title: Why are phone threats and sporadic intimidation rejected as constitutionally sufficient 'persecution' for asylum?
questions.question_body: The opinion notes that threats alone are insufficient to constitute persecution under the INA. I understand that physical harm is not required, but can someone explain the specific test for 'offensive' or 'serious' harm that the 10th Circuit uses? Does the court require the harm to rise above mere stress, and how is 'more than restrictions' measured in a case with no physical injury?

questions.title: How does the court apply the 'Central Reason' test when a Petitioner is harmed by multiple actors for multiple motives?
questions.question_body: Petitioners alleged persecution for two reasons: political opinion (Liberal Party) and criminal activity (Narco-guerrilla). The court found the political opinion was merely 'tangential.' If a Perpetrator has multiple motives, does political opinion still qualify if it is just one of many factors, and what evidence places the other motive above it as the 'dominant' reason for the harm?

questions.title: Does a Petitioner's status as a government lawyer or National Prosecutor office employee affect the Government Unwilling/Unable analysis?
questions.question_body: The opinion highlights that Petitioners worked for the government而在 the charge of reporting. The court notes that 'Without such reporting, there is no way to know how the police would have reacted.' If a Petitioner has a strong professional connection to the state, does that connection actually help them establish the government is 'unwilling' or 'unable' to help them protect the rest of the family?

questions.title: Is the testimony of unharmed family members in the home country sufficient to rebut a Presumption of Fear of Persecution?
questions.question_body: The court finds internal relocation safe because Petitioners have family members left in Colombia. However, does the presence of family members generally preclude a finding of 'unable or unwilling' government protection or safe relocation? Why does the court distinguish between the safety of the family and the safety of the Petitioner, and how is 'presumption of Well-Founded Fear' affected by the presence of 'unharmed' relatives?

questions.title: What is the difference between De Novo review and Substantial Evidence review for the Tenth Circuit when reviewing BIA asylum denials?
questions.question_body: I see the court mentions they review the BIA's findings of fact under the 'substantial-evidence standard' and are 'conclusive' unless compelling evidence exists. How does this relate to the idea that 'Petitioners fail to demonstrate a well-founded fear'? Does the substantial evidence standard prevent the court from deciding the case based on the Petitioner's own opinion of the evidence?

questions.title: Why does the failure to meet Asylum standards automatically result in a denial of Withholding of Removal in this case?
questions.question_body: The opinion concludes that because Petitioners fail to demonstrate a well-founded fear under asylum standards, they necessarily fail the higher standard for withholding of removal. If Withholding holds a higher standard of protection, why isn't the court required to independently review the evidence for Withholding or simply deny for lack of evidence rather than relying on the Asylum failure?
